evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Scope and behaviour are concrete and small enough to estimate (UI to enter name/description and create game).

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Clear, bounded functionality (generate/share URL) suitable for estimating.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specific UI action and outcome; implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Straightforward requirement to display a list of session items; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear selection behavior; sufficiently specified to estimate implementation effort.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Concrete add-item functionality; scope is small and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Edit functionality is precise enough to estimate effort.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Delete action is concrete and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Behavior (show estimates immediately) is specific enough to estimate implementation (toggle/permission logic).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Calculation and acceptance of average is well defined and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specific trigger and behaviour; implementation effort can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Simple action to set agreed estimate; bounded and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Clear behavior (re-estimate previously estimated story); implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Import lacks required details (accepted formats, column mapping, validation rules), making reasonable implementation estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste behavior is scoped and implementable (paste handling and parsing); estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing/listing previous games is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript is a bounded feature; implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export to HTML is a specific deliverable and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV export is a concrete output and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Delete semantics are clear (remove stored stories/estimates); implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation fields are explicit; feature scope is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Authentication by username/password is well understood and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Profile update functionality is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion (and cascade of games) is definable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display conversion is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reset via email is a well-defined feature; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Explicit option choices make the requirement concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A numeric limit is given, making scope clear and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining by entering a name at a provided URL is straightforward and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the current item is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Listing future session items is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicator for given estimates is defined enough to estimate implementation.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Trigger condition and behavior are explicit and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Clear timebox for change; behavior is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Displaying prior estimates for a story is a concrete feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing mapping of estimator -> estimate is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer duration and visibility are explicit; implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reset trigger and behavior are specified and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling/history viewing is bounded and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Ordering requirement is explicit and implementable; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Clear condition and behaviour; scope small enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: UI element and placement are specific enough to estimate effort.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards exist (XHTML/CSS); implementing compliance is definable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Unspecified scope (which terms, level of detail) makes it hard to estimate content creation effort.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: "as fast as possible" is an unbounded acceptance criterion and no target queries or performance goals are specified, making estimation uncertain.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browsers and versions are explicitly named; scope is clear enough to estimate cross-browser effort.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: "where possible" and which W3C accessibility criteria/level are not specified, leaving acceptance and effort underspecified.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: "quickly" is a subjective, unspecified performance target, preventing reliable estimation of required work.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Support for Unicode is a concrete technical requirement and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: "sensible and predictable" are subjective and acceptance criteria are not defined, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: "nice" is subjective and the expected content/coverage of error pages is unspecified, hindering reliable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Undefined term 'non-identifiable' and missing details on anonymization/pseudonymization means effort cannot be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: "some metrics" is vague (which metrics, granularity, time range), so scope is underspecified and not estimatable.
